Mu'adh had a new box of coloured pencils that his uncle had given him after a journey. It had twenty-four colours, and no one in the class had ever seen one like it.

Ghaith loved drawing, and he looked at that box every day.

When the school announced a drawing competition, Ghaith said to Mu'adh, "Will you lend me the gold pencil? I'll draw the sun in my picture with it, and give it back tomorrow."

Mu'adh gave him the pencil and said, "It's my favourite one, so be careful with it."

Ghaith drew a shining golden sun, and his picture won first prize.

He was so happy that he forgot the pencil in his school bag.

A day went by, then two days, then a week. Every time Ghaith saw the pencil in his bag, he said, "I'll give it back tomorrow."

Then he started drawing with it at home, until he almost thought it was his own.
Mu'adh would look at his box and see the empty space where the gold pencil belonged — but he felt too shy to ask his friend for it.

One day Ghaith went into his room and found his little brother Yahya colouring with his new eraser. Yahya had taken it days ago and not given it back.

Ghaith shouted, "That's my eraser! You took it and never gave it back!"

Yahya said, "I thought you'd forgotten about it."

Ghaith suddenly went quiet. He put his hand on his school bag and felt the gold pencil inside it.

And he remembered Mu'adh's face as he looked at his box.

In the morning he went to Mu'adh before the bell rang. He took out the pencil, along with a folded piece of paper, and said, "I'm sorry I took so long, Mu'adh. Please forgive me."

On the paper was a little drawing: a golden sun, and under it, "Thank you, my friend."

Mu'adh laughed and said, "I knew you'd bring it back."

Then he said, "You know what? The sun you drew is even nicer than the pencil itself."

From that day on, whenever Ghaith borrowed something, he gave it back the same day — and he wrote its owner's name on his hand so he would not forget.

﴿وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ لِأَمَانَاتِهِمْ وَعَهْدِهِمْ رَاعُونَ﴾

📖 Al-Mu'minun 8. This is a tale told as a parable; it did not happen to anyone in particular.
